# Alcohol Scripts about the Weekend

Weekends often carry strong “alcohol scripts.” These are unwritten rules or expectations like *“It’s the weekend, so I should drink,”* or *“This is my time to unwind.”*

These scripts develop through:

-   Routine (“Friday = drinks”)
-   Cultural messaging (weekends = celebration/reward)
-   Relief from work stress or boredom

Over time, the brain links: **Weekend → downtime → urge to drink**

Even for people choosing abstinence, these associations can trigger urges automatically, even if drinking no longer aligns with their goals.


![](https://github.com/jjcurtin/aud_support/blob/main/modules/images/happyweekend.png?raw=true){fig-align="center"}

::: callout
### Reflection

Take some time to reflect on the following prompts. It may be helpful to spend a few minutes responding in a journal.

1.  What does “the weekend” mean to me emotionally or mentally? What expectations do I notice about how weekends should look or feel? When I imagine a “good weekend,” what do I picture?

2.  What thoughts about drinking come up as the weekend approaches? Are there specific times (Friday night, Saturday afternoon, Sunday evening) that feel linked to alcohol?

3.  When I think about drinking on the weekend, what am I really wanting? Relief? Celebration? Disconnection? Comfort? Routine? What feelings tend to show up if I don’t drink?

4.  In my past experience, what has drinking on the weekend actually given me? What has it taken away or interfered with? How do I typically feel by the end of the weekend?

5.  If alcohol weren’t part of the picture, what would I want my weekends to feel like? What activities, environments, or people help create that feeling? What does rest or enjoyment actually look like for me?
:::
